rationale: Round 0 failed with a compiler internal error, so all weights are pulled into a moderate 0.15-0.55 band with no extreme highs or lows that could drive the pass pipeline into degenerate transformations. SUB remains the anchor pass: it is cheap, safe, and effective on this benchmark's arithmetic-heavy eigenvalue/QR code (Jacobi, QRiterate, HouseMatrix), so it keeps the highest security/diversity weights with the lowest cost and risk. BCF and FLA stay enabled but tempered (0.45-0.55 costs/risks) because this is a loop-dense numerical workload where bogus control flow and flattening hit the hot loops of Trianglelise, Jacobi, and QRiterate hardest, and aggressive flattening of large functions (3343-byte Trianglelise) is a plausible source of the prior internal error. SPLIT is kept light (0.25-0.35) as a low-risk size-friendly complement, IBR gets moderate opaque-predicate weight for branch-level diversity without heavy runtime cost, ICALL is moderate since indirect-call conversion on floating-point-heavy code adds modest overhead with some correctness sensitivity, and IGV stays mild for inter-procedural diversity. Overall the table favors safe arithmetic transformation, applies control-flow passes selectively, and preserves acceptable runtime and size on a 14 KB text binary.
